q: 1. For a cantilever with a uniformly distributed load, w over its entire length L, the maximum bending moment is
explain: The total load is wL acting at a distance L/2 from the fixed support. Thus, M = (wL) * (L/2) = wL²/2 at the fixed end.

q: 2. If the width b and depth d of a beam simply supported with a central load are interchanged, the deflection at the centre of the beam will be changed in the ratio of
explain: Since I ∝ bd³, swapping b and d changes I from bd³ to db³; the deflection ratio (inversely proportional to I) works out to (b/d)².

q: 3. The maximum deflection in the cantilever beam carrying a point load (W) at end is
explain: Standard structural formula for a cantilever with a point load at the free end: δ = WL³ / 3EI.

q: 4. The deflection of any rectangular beam simply supported, is
options: inversely proportional to the cube of its depth
directly proportional to the cube of its length
explain: Since deflection δ ∝ 1/I and I ∝ d³ for a rectangular section, deflection is inversely proportional to the cube of the beam's depth.

q: 5. In a cantilever beam a point load is applied at the free end. Which one is correct?
options: SF is uniform throughout the beam
SF varies linearly from free end to fixed end
BM is uniform throughout the beam
explain: Since there is only one load at the end and no other loads, the shear force remains constant (uniform) at value W across the entire length.

q: 6. Which of the following section is the most efficient in carrying bending moments?
explain: An I-section is most efficient because most of its area is located in the flanges, far from the neutral axis, providing a high Section Modulus (Z) for a given area.

q: 7. The bending moment is maximum on a section where shear force
explain: Mathematically, dM/dx = V. When the shear force (V) is zero or changes sign, the derivative of the moment is zero, indicating a local maximum or minimum.

q: 8. In a continuous bending moment curve the point where its changes sign is called
explain: The point where the bending moment changes sign (from sagging to hogging or vice versa) is known by all these terms in structural engineering.

q: 9. For any types of loading, the no. of point of contraflexture in a simply supported beam is
explain: In a simply supported beam, the bending moment usually maintains the same sign (sagging) throughout the span, so there are zero points of contraflexure.

q: 10. The moment diagram for a cantilever carrying concentrated load at its free end will be
explain: The moment varies linearly from 0 at the free end to WL at the fixed end, creating a triangular shape.

q: 11. Shear force for a cantilever carrying a uniformly distributed load over its whole length is
explain: The shear force varies linearly from 0 at the free end to wL at the fixed end, resulting in a triangular Shear Force Diagram.

q: 12. When a rectangular beam is loaded longitudinally, shear develops
explain: Longitudinal loading (axial) typically creates uniform stress, but internal shear can be considered present across horizontal planes depending on the distribution of load.

q: 13. If the shear force along a section of a beam is zero, the bending moment at the section is
explain: As dM/dx = V, if V=0, the bending moment is at a stationary point, which is typically the maximum (or minimum) value in the region.

q: 14. The arch meant for supporting uniformly distributed loads, to avoid any bending moment must be
explain: A parabolic arch is the 'funicular' shape for a uniformly distributed load, meaning it carries the load purely through compression with zero bending moment.

q: 15. The amount of bending moment induced in a cable is
explain: A perfectly flexible cable cannot resist bending; it carries loads through pure tension.

q: 16. For a beam of uniform strength, if width is constant
explain: Since bending stress σ ∝ M/(bd²) must remain constant with b fixed, d must vary as √M for uniform strength.

q: 17. Beams of composed of more than one material, rigidly connected together so as to be one piece are known as
explain: Beams made of two or more different materials rigidly bonded together to act as a single unit are termed composite beams.

q: 18. The maximum deflection due due to load W at the free end of a cantilever of length L and having flexural rigidity EI is
explain: For a cantilever with a point load W at the free end, the standard maximum tip deflection formula is WL³/3EI.

q: 19. Find the DSI of propped cantilever beam
explain: A propped cantilever has 4 reaction components (3 at fixed end + 1 at prop). With 3 equilibrium equations, the Degree of Static Indeterminacy (DSI) is $$4 - 3 = 1$$.

q: 20. The simultaneous equations of slope deflection method can be solved by iteration in
explain: The Moment Distribution Method is essentially an iterative procedure for solving the same equations found in the slope-deflection method.

q: 21. Slope deflection method is
explain: The Slope Deflection method is a displacement (deflection) method of structural analysis that relates end moments to joint rotations and displacements.

q: 22. Slope deflection method is
explain: The slope deflection method is a 'displacement method' or 'deflection method' where unknown joint displacements (slopes and deflections) are treated as the primary unknowns.

q: 23. A simply supported beam is subjected to a pure moment. This will be resisted through
options: a moment reaction at hinged end
a moment reaction at hinge on rollers end
a couple formed by the reaction from the two supports
external support capable of resisting moment which is necessarily to be provided
explain: Since hinge/roller supports cannot resist moment directly, an applied pure moment on a simply supported beam is instead balanced by a couple formed from equal and opposite vertical reactions at the two supports.

q: 24. A cantilever beam is the one which is supported with
options: one end hinge and other on rollers
one end fixed and the other on rollers
one end fixed and the other free
explain: By definition, a cantilever beam is fixed (built-in) at one end while the other end is completely free.

q: 25. Which of the following beams will have points of contraflexure?
options: A simply supported beam with udl over entire span
An overhanging beam with loading only over supported span and not on overhangs
Fixed beam subjected to concentrated load
Cantilever subjected to uniformly varying loads
explain: A fixed beam under a concentrated load develops both hogging moments near supports and sagging moment mid-span, so the bending moment changes sign, creating points of contraflexure.

q: 26. A beam is said to have been subjected to a pure bending moment, when
options: the load is applied as a udl throughout the span
S.F. in a length is zero
the load is applied at the mid-span section only
explain: Pure bending occurs over a length where shear force is zero (since dM/dx = SF), leaving only a constant bending moment.

q: 27. The assumption that the cross-sections plane before bending remain plane even after bending means
options: the strains in the fibers are proportional to their distances from neutral axis
the bending moment will be resisted by the central core of the section
the stresses in the fibres are proportional to their distances from neutral axis
the neutral axis lies at mid height
explain: Plane sections remaining plane implies a linear variation of strain with distance from the neutral axis, which is the fundamental Bernoulli-Euler bending assumption.

q: 28. The line of thrust of the linear arch is
options: the imaginary line of thrust for a given set of loads
explain: For a given set of loads, the linear arch (or theoretical arch) follows the shape of the funicular polygon, which represents the imaginary line of thrust.

q: 29. The assumption in the theory of bending that the material is homogeneous and isotropic has the same value of Young's Modulus in tension and compression implies that
options: the stresses are proportional to strains at all fibres
the strains are proportional to distances of the fibres from neutral axis
the beam bends into a circular arc
the neutral axis lies at the centre
explain: Equal E in tension and compression (homogeneous, isotropic material) combined with Hooke's law implies stress is proportional to strain uniformly at all fibres of the section.

q: 30. If there is a cantilever beam joined with the edge of the span, then it is
explain: Joining a cantilever to an existing span introduces additional redundant constraints or internal forces that cannot be solved by simple static equilibrium equations alone, making the structure indeterminate.

q: 31. Influence line is
options: the line showing stress function due to unit moving load
the line showing stress function due to unit load
the line showing stress function due to udl
explain: By definition, an Influence Line Diagram (ILD) represents the variation of a specific response (stress function like shear, moment, or reaction) at a fixed section as a unit load moves across the structure.

q: 32. Which one is right w.r.t. ILD?
options: it is the BMD due to unit load
it is the BMD due to static unit load
it is the BMD due to moving unit load
it is the BMD due to impacting unit load
explain: The ILD specifically captures the effects of a moving unit load. Unlike a standard BMD which shows the effect of a fixed load along the whole beam, the ILD shows the effect at one spot for all possible load positions.

q: 33. The influence line diagram for S.F. or BM at a section is
options: the value of S.F. or B.M. at that section when the unit load is placed over that section only
the value of S.F. or B.M. at that section when the unit load is at the centre of the span
the variation in the value of S.F. or B.M. at that section as the unit load transverses the span from left to right
explain: An ILD for a section must show the full range of variation (the 'influence') as the unit load moves from the start of the span to the end.

q: 34. The influence line diagram for reaction at a support of a simply supported beam is
options: a triangle with ordinate 1 at that support
a triangle with ordinate 1 at the other support
explain: For a support reaction $R_A$, the reaction is 1 when the unit load is exactly at A, and 0 when it is at the other support B. This creates a right-angled triangle with a peak (ordinate) of 1 at support A.

q: 35. The influence line diagram for reaction at the support of a cantilever will be a
options: triangle with zero ordinate at fixed end and unit ordinate at free end
triangle with unit ordinate at fixed end and zero ordinate at free end
explain: In a cantilever, any vertical load placed anywhere on the beam must be fully resisted by the single vertical reaction at the fixed support. Therefore, the reaction is always 1, resulting in a rectangle with unit ordinate.

q: 36. The influence line diagram for shear force at a section on a cantilever will be
options: a rectangle of length equal to full length of span with unit ordinate
a rectangle extending between free end and the section with unit ordinate
a triangle extending for whole length of span with unit ordinate at fixed support
a triangle extending between the section and the fixed end with unit ordinate at fixed support
explain: Shear force at a section in a cantilever only exists when the load is between the free end and that section. If the load is between the fixed support and the section, the shear at that section is zero. This creates a rectangle from the section to the free end.

q: 37. The influence line diagram for BM at a section in a cantilever will be a triangle extending between the section and the
options: fixed end with maximum ordinate under the section
fixed end with maximum ordinate under the fixed end
unsupported end with maximum ordinate at the section
unsupported end with maximum ordinate at the supported end
explain: The bending moment at a section is created by the load multiplied by its distance from that section. The maximum moment occurs when the unit load is at the farthest possible point from the support (the free/unsupported end).

q: 38. The influence line diagram for BM at a section of a simply supported beam will be a
options: triangle with maximum ordinate at the section and zero at the two supports
triangle with maximum ordinate at the support nearer to the section and zero at the other support
explain: For a simply supported beam, the B.M. at a section 'C' is zero when the load is at either support and reaches its maximum value (ab/L) when the load is directly on the section.

q: 39. A beam is a structural member predominantly subjected to
explain: A beam, by definition, is a structural member designed to primarily resist transverse (perpendicular to its axis) loads, developing shear and bending.

q: 40. A beam is completely analyzed when
options: shear and moment diagrams are found
the moment of inertia is uniform throughout the length
explain: A beam analysis is considered complete once the shear force and bending moment diagrams (which describe internal forces along the entire length) are obtained.

q: 41. In general equation for the deflection of the beam: M=EI*  where EI is
explain: EI represent the flexural strength.

q: 42. A rigid frame is a structure composed of members which are connected by
explain: By definition, a rigid frame has members connected by rigid (moment-resisting) joints, as opposed to pin-jointed trusses.

q: 43. When the load does not pass through the shear centre of the steel beam. It produces
options: torsional moment along with bending moment
explain: Loads not passing through the shear center cause twisting (torsion). The resistance to this is related to the torsional and sectional rigidity of the beam.

q: 44. A frame is completely analyzed when
options: the variation in shear is found throughout the frame
the variation in direct stress, shear and moment is found throughout the frame
the shear and moment reaction from member to member are known at every joint
explain: A rigid frame analysis is complete only when all three internal force quantities—axial (direct) force, shear force, and bending moment—are known throughout every member.

q: 45. When a cantilever beam of length l is loaded with a uniformly varying load of maximum intensity w at free end, the shape of bending moment diagram is
explain: Since the load is linear (varying), the shear force is parabolic ($x^2$), and the bending moment is a cubic function ($x^3$).

explain: At a simple end support or hinge, the internal bending moment is zero.

q: 47. The slope and the deflection at a section in a loaded beam cannot be found out by :
explain: Rankine's method is typically used for earth pressure or column buckling, not for determining beam deflection.

q: 48. For the beam shown in figure, the shear force at A is equal to (refer to image 1667):
explain: For a beam with a triangular load (zero at A, peak at B), the total load is $wl/2$ and the reaction at the lighter end A is $wl/6$.

q: 49. Prestressing to a large extent removes the disadvantages which a conventional reinforced concrete structure suffers as compared to a comparable :
explain: Prestressing allows concrete to span longer distances and remain crack-free, making it competitive with steel structures.

q: 50. For a cantilever with a uniformly distributed load of total W over entire length L, the max bending moment is :
explain: If W is the total load ($w \cdot L$), the moment at the fixed end is $W \cdot (L/2) = WL/2$.
